title: What If The Power Went Out For 3 Days?
sources: American Red Cross, Power Outage Safety (fridge keeps food cold ~4 hours if unopened; a full freezer ~48 hours; use flashlights, not candles; disconnect electronics to avoid surge damage)
Ready.gov, Water (store at least one gallon of water per person per day)

lines.text: What would you do if the power went out for three whole days?
lines.caps: What would *you | do if the *power | went *out?

lines.text: It's nine at night, and suddenly everything goes dark.
Step one: don't touch the fridge.
If you keep it closed, your food stays cold for about four hours, and a full freezer lasts two days.
lines.caps: Keep it *closed | food stays *cold | about four *hours | a full *freezer | lasts two *days.

lines.text: Step two: grab a flashlight, not a candle.
Candles and dark rooms are a real fire risk.
Step three: fill some bottles with water,
about a gallon per person, every day.
because when the power comes back, a surge can fry them.
Day three: the lights flicker back on.
And because you were ready, you're totally fine.
